title: Adaptive client heartbeat, drain window, and distributed consensus for partial-output reconciliation
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: When clients disconnect mid-generation (network blips, process crash, or deliberate cancel), the runtime currently relies on fixed timeouts and unilateral heuristics to reclaim resources and garbage collect KV prefixes. This causes either premature eviction (losing resumable output) or long tail resource retention. We also need to ensure correctness when tool/function calls produce structured output mid-stream.

Goal: Implement an adaptive heartbeat + drain-window protocol with lightweight distributed consensus metadata so the gateway, runtime workers, and caching layer agree on ownership and can deterministically reconcile partial generations without leaking resources or losing resumable state. Must be backwards-compatible with older SDK clients that only support simple 'disconnect' semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can reclaim orphaned generation state within configurable drain windows without dropping resumable prefixes for healthy reconnects.
Gateway and workers exchange compact ownership epochs so reconnection logic can validate resumption tokens and avoid split-brain.

System supports in-stream function/tool calls: if a tool call is pending when the client disconnects, the result is either committed to a durable partial output or the call is canceled consistently across components.
No regression in 99th percentile latency for short streaming calls (<3s).
Compatibility shim allows older SDKs to reconnect with reduced guarantees (best-effort resumption) and logs a deprecation telemetry event.
tech_notes: Design overview: each generation (request) gets an ownership tuple <owner_id, epoch, drain_deadline>. Owners (gateway instance that accepted request) send heartbeats to local coord service every H ms; when gateway moves ownership (scale, restart), epoch increments atomically via central metadata store (consensus via lightweight leader-backed sequence number). Drain window: on graceful client close, owner sets drain_deadline = now + D, during which resumption tokens remain valid; after drain_deadline expired and no heartbeat, a lease release process marks fragments eligible for GC. For partial outputs with tools: implement a small durable 'pending-tool' ledger entry linked to generation; either worker commits result atomically with the fragment or garbage-collects if lease lost. Trade-offs: central sequence reduces corner-case divergence but adds a very small write on ownership change; alternative was fully-distributed vector-timestamp which increased complexity for rare cases.
implementation_plan: Add lightweight ownership metadata service (leader-backed sequence) in control plane (runtime-1.20).
Extend generation metadata schema with owner_id, epoch, drain_deadline, pending_tool_id.
Gateway: emit heartbeats and implement graceful close API that sets drain_deadline.
Worker: honor epoch on resume attempts, reject resume if epoch mismatch, and support 'steal' flow only when epoch advanced and GC window expired.
KV/Cache: add 'lease' flag per-prefix tied to owner tuple; GC process consults epoch and drain_deadline.
SDK compatibility: add an SDK handshake flag 'supports_adaptive_drain' and a client-side reconnection fallback.
Instrument telemetry for heartbeat rates, epoch changes, and orphaned-state counts.
migration_plan: Roll out ownership metadata and drain window in canary across a single region; enable journal writes only on ownership changes to minimize write amplification. Gate SDK feature by 'supports_adaptive_drain' and fallback to existing behavior if missing. Plan two-week observation window then widen rollout.
test_plan: Unit tests: epoch increment and validation, drain_deadline calculations, pending_tool commit/cancel paths.
Integration: simulate gateway restart during active generation and verify resume token validation and GC timing.
Chaos: kill gateway mid-tool-call and ensure tool ledger either commits or cancels deterministically.
Performance: load test 100k short streaming requests to validate no P99 latency regression.
comments: 2026-02-26 — Avery Chen: Initial draft of proposal posted. Need architecture review from infra and SDK teams. Tagged Marco for implementation planning.

2026-03-02 — Marco Singh: Implemented preliminary ownership tuple and heartbeat in gateway prototype. Observed ~0.2% increase in gateway CPU for H=250ms; lowering to 1s reduces CPU but increases detection latency. Added experiment notes to PR.

2026-03-07 — Lena Ortiz (SDK): Reviewed compatibility shim. Suggest exposing a 'reconnection_strength' enum to let clients express tolerance for resumption guarantees. PM and security ok with telemetry.
2026-03-10 — Marco Singh: Worker changes merged to staging (PR #2418). Worker now rejects resume attempts if epoch mismatch and returns structured error with 'resume_compat_hint'.
2026-03-12 — QA: Found flaky test where drain_deadline rounding caused premature GC in low-latency clocks; fixed by using monotonic clocks across components.
2026-03-14 — Avery Chen: Preparing canary rollout in us-west-2. Creating runtime-1.20 canary job and scheduling observations for two full business days.
